one_line: A shared release room where agents verify evidence and humans approve shipping.
what_it_does: Coordinates independent build, risk, and customer checks for a release, surfaces conflicts, and stages a human-reviewed resolution.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes domain-level release inspection and verification against the same live state the owner watches; a pixel-driving agent would be materially less reliable for evidence reconciliation and the human approval boundary.
leverage_evidence: About text describes get_release_case, run_release_verification, get_release_conflicts, and prepare_owner_resolution tools.
Video frames show a shared Release 2.4.0 workspace with independent Build, Risk, and Customer agent checks.
Human-only Approve & seal boundary and activity stream are part of the stated workflow.
execution_rationale: The frames show a coherent release dashboard and distinct verification tracks, but do not clearly show the full verification-to-seal flow or underlying evidence details.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show consistent release-room UI and multiple agent check cards.
Visible statuses suggest a prepared release state.
No readable final approval, shipping result, or detailed tool trace is shown.
impact_rationale: Release owners and engineering teams have a concrete need to reconcile build, security, and customer readiness evidence before shipping; the product directly addresses that coordination problem.
impact_evidence: Pitch centers on scattered release decisions across CI, security, support, and private context.
Shared evidence and contradiction surfacing are visible in the described workflow.
creativity_rationale: The explicit agent verification room with a human-only shipping boundary is a fresh, memorable application of WebMCP beyond generic CRUD automation.
creativity_evidence: Independent role-based agents verify one launch claim and surface contradictions.
Decision receipt becomes available only after human approval.
usability_note: The release-room structure and role cards are legible, though evidence details are small in the frame sheets.
red_flags: Frame sheets are repetitive and do not visibly complete human approval and shipping.
advance_reason: Strong concept and clear product surface with meaningful WebMCP leverage; execution evidence is good but not fully end-to-end.

one_line: A live brand-conversation benchmark explorer for human and agent co-analysis.
what_it_does: Lets users and agents browse a portfolio of real brands and games, compare versioned scores, drill into findings, and prepare reports.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools let an agent navigate live benchmark data, update comparisons, and investigate findings while the human sees the same visual state; generic UI driving would be less precise and reliable for multi-step exploration.
leverage_evidence: About text states the live site exposes 15+ WebMCP tools over a 79-title real-brand portfolio.
Frames show changing benchmark/category views and comparison dashboards.
Description explicitly shows an agent selecting titles and writing them into the live comparison.
execution_rationale: The product appears polished and data-rich with multiple coherent views, though the montage does not make every tool call or final report legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show consistent dark benchmark dashboards, title collections, scores, and category views.
Visible workflow includes comparison and drill-down states.
Devpost packaging includes multiple gallery images and a live demo.
impact_rationale: Brand, game, and product teams can use customer-conversation benchmarks and version comparisons for concrete research and decision support.
impact_evidence: Description identifies real customers and a 79-title portfolio.
Frames show versioned scores, categories, and comparative views useful to analysts.
creativity_rationale: Human-plus-agent exploration of live brand conversation data is a strong synthesis, though the underlying benchmark dashboard category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent independently picks a fast-climbing app and rivals and writes them into the live comparison.
Rendered brief and tool trail are presented beside the visual data explorer.
usability_note: Rich visual dashboards and comparison views appear usable, but dense screenshots make some labels and transitions hard to verify.
red_flags: Frame montage is repetitive and exact tool traces are small.
advance_reason: Credible live-data product with substantial structured exploration and visible results.

one_line: A storefront that asks the highest-value clarifying question instead of guessing.
what_it_does: Searches a large catalog, parses natural-language constraints, quantifies ambiguity, asks one discriminating question when needed, and returns products when evidence is sufficient.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets the storefront return structured uncertainty and the next best question from its catalog distribution, changing the agent from a guesser into a grounded conversational shopper; generic UI automation cannot reliably reproduce this contract.
leverage_evidence: search_products returns either an answer or need_more_evidence with the question, options, counts, and reason.
Description covers constraint parsing, category traversal, change-of-mind handling, and no-result recovery.
Frames show iterative storefront query/result states.
execution_rationale: The concept and storefront workflow appear substantially implemented with consistent product cards and query states, though the montage does not clearly show one fully legible clarification loop end to end.
execution_evidence: Frames show populated catalog results across multiple states.
About text describes 9,901 real products and concrete ambiguity statistics.
Public live demo and repository are listed.
impact_rationale: Shoppers routinely face ambiguous catalogs and poor recommendations; asking a useful clarifying question is a credible improvement for commerce agents.
impact_evidence: Description gives concrete belt and shoe search examples with candidate counts.
Product aims to prevent presenting a coin-flip ranking as an answer.
creativity_rationale: Treating uncertainty and information gain as a first-class storefront response is unusually original and deeply pursued in the interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Storefront declines to guess and chooses the question that clears the most candidates.
Natural-language requirements, refusals, ceilings, and changed minds are explicitly modeled.
usability_note: The question-first interaction is promising and product-oriented, although frame text is too small to verify details.
red_flags: Clarification call sequence and exact outputs are not fully legible in the contact sheet.
advance_reason: One of the clearest and most original WebMCP interaction models, with credible commerce value.

one_line: A shared circuit-troubleshooting workspace where agent reasoning and simulation stay together.
what_it_does: Combines a circuit simulator with measurements, hypotheses, diagnostic steps, repair testing, and agent actions in one synchronized workspace.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to the current circuit, measurements, hypotheses, and simulation lets an agent act on exact engineering state rather than reconstructing screenshots and chat context.
leverage_evidence: About text lists tools for inspecting circuits, measuring, proposing or implementing repairs, and verifying in simulation.
Frames show a circuit canvas changing through editing/testing states.
Shared activity and workspace state are central to the pitch.
execution_rationale: The montage visibly progresses from sparse workspace to an assembled/evaluated circuit, but numerical measurements, diagnostics, and explicit agent calls are not readable.
execution_evidence: Frames show schematic editing, configuration panels, and a changing circuit/output state.
Devpost description aligns the interface with reasoning, measuring, testing, and refining.
No clear readable end-to-end diagnosis or measurement result is shown.
impact_rationale: Circuit debugging is a real, difficult task for electronics learners and practitioners, and preserving circuit state while testing repairs offers direct value.
impact_evidence: Description identifies fragmented workflows across schematics, measurements, datasheets, simulation, and help.
Frames show a dedicated simulator workspace rather than a generic chat.
creativity_rationale: Turning a circuit simulator into a shared agent-human troubleshooting environment is a distinctive interaction model with meaningful technical ambition.
creativity_evidence: Reasoning, measurements, hypotheses, repairs, and simulation are combined in one workspace.
Agent can implement and verify repairs rather than only advise.
usability_note: The workspace is coherent for a technical user, but small frame text and unclear measurements limit confidence.
red_flags: No legible agent transcript, tool trace, or quantitative simulation result.
advance_reason: Strong domain fit and novel shared workspace; evidence supports a working prototype but not complete diagnostic depth.

one_line: A calm ambient display that agents can safely recompose without overriding human intent.
what_it_does: Shows ambient scenes, weather, approved web content, and priority messages through structured tools while preserving touch interaction and undo boundaries.
leverage_rationale: High-level named actions and state inspection are substantially more reliable than pixel/gesture automation against a cinematic distant-view display, while the same controllers serve human and agent actions.
leverage_evidence: About text lists seven tools for state inspection, weather, information, approved transport page, messages, return, and undo.
Frames show transitions from ambient clock to weather, web, and meeting views with activity evidence.
Description emphasizes schema-validated intent rather than DOM guessing.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence shows a coherent, polished set of display state transitions and a human-first safety model, though physical hardware and edge cases are not shown.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly show ambient, weather, web, and notification states.
Agent/activity panel accompanies the display changes.
URL validation and same-origin mapping are described.
impact_rationale: Ambient displays have a clear niche audience and the ability to safely request useful context or notifications without losing touch control is credible value.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets always-on 4K OLED/touch displays.
Frames show concrete weather, transport, and meeting use cases.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a distant, gesture-driven ambient display with explicit human authority is a memorable and well-integrated interaction concept.
creativity_evidence: Agent recomposes the same physical-display experience through named intents.
Undo is constrained to the most recent agent action and human touch remains available.
usability_note: Calm visual presentation and explicit modes are approachable; the frame montage is repetitive.
red_flags: No clear physical-device footage or failure-path evidence.
advance_reason: Polished, concrete demonstration of WebMCP improving a difficult-to-automate display surface.

one_line: A public adversarial range that tests WebMCP agents against prompt injection and scope creep.
what_it_does: Presents hidden and explicit tool traps, records agent interactions, recomputes outcomes server-side, and emits signed tamper-evident scorecards.
leverage_rationale: The product exists specifically to expose and evaluate the structured agent-tool surface; WebMCP is not an add-on but the tested attack surface and measurement interface.
leverage_evidence: Description lists poisoned descriptions, typosquatted names, prompt injection in results, scope creep, and multi-step attacks.
Frames show tool/task panels, execution evidence, and a 5/6 scorecard.
Server-side recomputation and signing make interaction events the core product state.
execution_rationale: The montage shows a clear run from adversarial scenarios through logged outcomes to a scorecard, with visible 5/6 results; cryptographic verification details are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show challenge screens, tool/result areas, and a final 5/6 score.
About text describes 17 registered tools, server-side logging, D1, and signed sealing.
Offline verifier and scorecard are presented as distinct product surfaces.
impact_rationale: As agents gain structured tool access, a public repeatable security range addresses a real safety and evaluation need for developers and organizations.
impact_evidence: Each trap maps to OWASP LLM Top 10 or MITRE ATLAS.
Public range and signed evidence support comparable security testing.
creativity_rationale: A cryptographically verifiable adversarial range for WebMCP is a novel, ambitious use of the medium and directly addresses an emerging attack surface.
creativity_evidence: Hidden prompt-injection and scope-creep traps are mixed with legitimate tools.
Score is recomputed from the event log and signed rather than trusting client claims.
usability_note: The testing flow and score are understandable, but dense screens make individual traps difficult to inspect.
red_flags: Observed run is 5/6 rather than perfect; detailed signature verification is not legible in the montage.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated agent-infrastructure project with end-to-end adversarial testing evidence.

one_line: An agent-ready 3D desk configurator where humans own taste and approval.
what_it_does: Combines Shopify discovery with a shared 3D desk world, preserves locked human choices, rejects stale proposals, and stages exact reviewable cart outcomes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides precise structured state and optimistic concurrency for a non-DOM 3D workspace, enabling an agent to discover, validate, and stage changes without overwriting concurrent human edits.
leverage_evidence: About text describes reading current scene, exact product IDs, visible parcels, locks, stale-call rejection, and versioned review.
Frames show the 3D desk configurator, accessory state, and review-oriented commerce surfaces.
Digest-bound, expiring, single-use approval is explicitly part of the flow.
execution_rationale: The product surface is polished and the stated workflow handles concurrency and consequential actions thoughtfully, but the frame montage does not visibly prove the full stale-call and Shopify path.
execution_evidence: Frames show coherent 3D desk scene, product details, and review states.
Description specifies locked lamp/keyboard behavior, conflict response, and partial-cart blocking.
Public repository and live demo are listed.
impact_rationale: Multi-product desk setup is a concrete commerce problem involving budget, variants, availability, and user taste; the product credibly reduces coordination burden.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies exact setup, budget, availability, and cart-reproduction pain points.
Human review and partial-cart safeguards address real purchase risk.
creativity_rationale: The shared miniature desk world, human locks, conflict-aware agent proposals, and digest-bound commerce approval form an unusually deep interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agent operates a non-DOM 3D world while preserving concurrent human edits.
Clear division of taste, repetitive discovery, state correctness, and approval responsibilities.
usability_note: The 3D scene and equivalent accessible list support direct manipulation, though the contact sheet is too small to inspect controls.
red_flags: Frames do not clearly show the agent trace, stale-call rejection, or final Shopify result.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and ambition for agent-mediated commerce, with a credible polished product surface.

one_line: A live booking site where the agent prepares the reservation and the human keeps the final click.
what_it_does: Exposes services, live availability, and booking preparation through WebMCP, then requires explicit human confirmation before committing the real booking.
leverage_rationale: Structured service and availability tools avoid brittle DOM scraping and let the agent perform the tedious, precise preparation while the page retains the consequential confirmation boundary.
leverage_evidence: Frames show tool registration, check_availability, booking preparation, confirmation card, and success.
About text specifies six home-page tools and four on other pages, with UTC-offset slots.
Agent is explicitly unable to click Confirm.
execution_rationale: The montage provides unusually clear end-to-end evidence from tool registration and availability through human confirmation and booking success.
execution_evidence: Frames show structured tool calls and returned availability, then a confirmation card with Confirm/Decline.
Final state reports booked and human-confirmed.
Live business/demo and public repository are listed.
impact_rationale: Businesses and customers have a direct need for reliable scheduling; the agent removes form-filling friction while preserving consent for a real calendar/inbox commitment.
impact_evidence: Description identifies a real booking service and genuinely bookable 30-minute windows.
Workflow ends in a human-confirmed booking and apparent email confirmation.
creativity_rationale: The human-keeps-the-click pattern is a strong, practical interaction model for agent-native services, though booking itself is a familiar category.
creativity_evidence: Explicit no-DOM-scraping flow with page-defined tools.
Decline is a first-class result and final commit is held outside agent control.
usability_note: The flow is easy to understand and the confirmation card makes the approval boundary clear.
red_flags: Failure paths and cancellation/error handling are not demonstrated.
advance_reason: Highly convincing live booking workflow with concrete WebMCP traces and successful human-authorized result.

one_line: A permissioned shared game where an AI agent becomes a real player.
what_it_does: Lets humans invite role-scoped agents into synchronized mini-chess sessions, with server-authoritative permissions, turns, legal moves, and results.
leverage_rationale: A general UI-driving agent would struggle to participate reliably in synchronized, permissioned game state; WebMCP makes the agent a first-class player under the same rules as humans.
leverage_evidence: About text describes page-defined tools to read rules, join, inspect state, wait for turn, and submit moves.
Frames show invitation/waiting UI, shared board, and agent-oriented interaction surfaces.
Server authority over identity, role, legal moves, turn order, and revisions is explicit.
execution_rationale: The board, invitation, and waiting states are coherent, but the supplied frames do not clearly show an agent joining, making a move, and changing the shared board.
execution_evidence: Frames show a rendered mini-chess board and waiting-for-agent state.
Devpost demo and mobile product screens are visible.
No readable move trace or completed game result is shown.
impact_rationale: The product offers credible entertainment and social value to players who want agents as opponents or participants, though the visible proof of the full play loop is limited.
impact_evidence: Pitch supports human-versus-agent and agent-versus-agent play with spectators.
Shared synchronized game state and invitations are shown conceptually.
creativity_rationale: Turning an agent from adviser into an invited, permissioned participant in a shared game is a memorable and extensible interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Role-scoped invitations and live synchronization are central, not cosmetic.
Two independent agents can occupy opposing seats while humans observe.
usability_note: The game concept is approachable, but narrow mobile frames and waiting-state repetition obscure the complete flow.
red_flags: Key move execution and synchronized before/after board state are not visibly demonstrated.
advance_reason: Very high leverage and creativity, with moderate execution evidence that warrants advancement.

one_line: An AI and browser collaborate to pack a constrained carry-on without sharing a user profile.
what_it_does: Reads an anonymous item catalog, lets an AI choose item IDs, packs them into a 6x8 suitcase under an 8 kg limit, and preserves user locks across repacks.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP creates a precise shared contract: the agent chooses anonymous item IDs while the page enforces physical fit, weight, and user locks; generic text recommendations cannot guarantee these constraints.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies 18 catalog items, 8 kg limit, 6x8 grid, user Keep locks, and browser-enforced constraints.
Frames show AI permission step, item catalog, suitcase layout, and changing packing score.
No profile, identity, prompt, or reasoning is accepted by the page.
execution_rationale: The visual sequence shows progressive filling and score improvement to roughly 93, with a coherent privacy and constraint story, though exact final weight and tool traces are not legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show empty-to-packed suitcase states and changing score/status.
Privacy statement and AI handoff are visible.
Devpost packaging identifies a WebMCP Smart Packing Demo.
impact_rationale: Travelers have a concrete packing burden under weight and space constraints; the product turns a recommendation into a visibly validated physical arrangement while respecting privacy.
impact_evidence: Pitch frames packing as tangible collaboration rather than another text list.
Visual suitcase result and 8 kg/6x8 constraints directly match the user need.
creativity_rationale: The privacy-preserving split between AI judgment and browser-enforced physical constraints is a fresh, memorable use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: AI chooses what matters while the page makes it fit.
User locks survive later AI repacks and only anonymous IDs are exchanged.
usability_note: The suitcase visualization and progressive score make the outcome understandable, though exact controls are small.
red_flags: Exact tool invocation and final constraint values are not readable in the montage.
advance_reason: Clear real-world use case with strong shared-state leverage and visible iterative outcome.
